relations.subject: Sylvain Lévi

relations.subject: Paul Eugène Pelliot
relations.evidence: In early 1900, Pelliot moved to Hanoi to take up a position as a research scholar at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (EFEO, "French School of the Far East").

relations.subject: Paul Eugène Pelliot
relations.evidence: In 1901, when only 23 years old, Pelliot was made a professor of Chinese at the EFEO.

relations.subject: Paul Eugène Pelliot
relations.role: chair in Languages, History, and Archaeology of Central Asia
relations.evidence: In 1911, at the age of just 33, a chair in Languages, History, and Archaeology of Central Asia was created for him at the prestigious Collège de France.

relations.subject: Paul Eugène Pelliot
relations.evidence: In 1920, Pelliot joined Henri Cordier as co-editor of the preeminent sinological journal T'oung Pao, serving until 1942. After Cordier's death in 1924

relations.subject: Paul Eugène Pelliot
relations.evidence: Pelliot edited T'oung Pao alone until he was joined by Dutch sinologist J. J. L. Duyvendak in 1932.
